description: Full-page layout skeletons at five levels (Entry, Hub, Index, Detail, Utility) for consumer and SaaS web products. Each template says what the page is for, how people reach it, how it changes at phone, tablet and desktop widths, which overlays and states it has, and which density tier it sits in. A template is a skeleton: the routed PATH rules decide the content, and they win where the two differ. Layouts only. Spacing, row heights and hit areas are token names, never values. Built from the interactive wireframe set; the Mobbin references are the screens each layout was drawn from.

levels.name: Entry
levels.meaning: Front door. Explains the product and gets a signup.

levels.name: Hub
levels.meaning: Where people land after signing in, or a page that sells one thing.

levels.name: Index
levels.meaning: A list of things in one section.

levels.name: Utility
levels.meaning: A page people visit rarely: settings, team, invoices, contact.

dense.desktop: Table rows use --table-row-h-dense. Block gaps use the tight steps.
dense.touch: Rows use --table-row-h-regular. Targets reach --hit-area-min. Block gaps go up one step.

standard.desktop: Rows use --table-row-h-regular. Gaps use the mid steps.
standard.touch: Same rows and gaps. Side gutter drops to the phone gutter.

spacious.desktop: Sections sit far apart with large type. Rows, where present, use --table-row-h-comfortable.
spacious.touch: Gaps step down one notch but stay looser than Standard. Tap targets reach --hit-area-min.

density.note: Values come from vois_get_tokens. This file names the token and the direction, never a number.

responsive.phone: Single column. Buttons stack to full width. Logos wrap to three per row. Plans stack, so put the recommended plan first. Footer links sit in two columns.
responsive.tablet: Hero stays stacked with the product shot under the text. Feature cards go two across. Pricing keeps three plans side by side.
responsive.desktop: Two column hero. Features three across. Split sections put image and text side by side. Five column footer.

templates.density_note: The hero heading is the biggest type on any page here, and sections sit far apart on desktop.

templates.name: Dashboard
templates.purpose: The landing page inside a SaaS product. It answers what changed and what needs attention.
templates.navigation: Left sidebar with labels on desktop, an icon rail on tablet, a bottom tab bar on phones. Search and account sit in the top bar.

responsive.phone: Sidebar becomes a bottom bar with four tabs and More. Metrics go two across. Chart and activity stack. The table turns into stacked rows: name as the title, with status and the other values under it. Nothing is dropped.
responsive.tablet: Icon rail. Metrics two across. Chart takes the full width with activity underneath. The table keeps all its columns.
responsive.desktop: Full sidebar. Four metrics in a row. Chart takes two thirds with activity beside it. Full table.

states.name: Default
states.what: Metric cards open a report. Rows jump to a record. View all opens the full list.

states.name: Notifications panel
states.what: The bell opens a right side panel. The page behind stays visible, so people keep their place.

states.name: Quick create modal
states.what: Create opens a small modal. A few fields at most, then it closes and the new item shows up in the list.

templates.interaction: View all goes to the Records section, then a row goes to the record. A table row on the dashboard skips the section and jumps straight to the record. That shortcut is fine, but the breadcrumb on the record should still show where it lives. The bell opens a side panel and Create opens a modal.
templates.density_note: Dense on desktop for scanning many metrics. On touch widths the same screen gets regular rows and more space between blocks.

mobbin_references.title: Browserbase overview
mobbin_references.note: Shortcut cards, then recent sessions, then analytics.

mobbin_references.title: Canny home
mobbin_references.note: Icon rail with big number cards under a welcome line.

mobbin_references.title: Mintlify home
mobbin_references.note: Thin icon rail and a single focus card with an activity list.

templates.name: Collection table
templates.purpose: A list of records people scan, filter, and act on in bulk.
templates.navigation: Same sidebar shell. Search sits left in the toolbar above the table. Filter and Sort are pinned top right. A row opens a preview panel on desktop and a full detail page on smaller screens.

responsive.phone: Rows turn into stacked cards with the name, status, and one line of detail. Filter and Sort stay pinned top right. Filter opens a full screen panel because filters include text fields. New record becomes a floating button and opens full screen, since it has text inputs.
responsive.tablet: Table has four columns on every width, so nothing is hidden. Filter and Sort stay pinned top right, with applied filters as chips under the toolbar. No preview panel, so rows open the detail page.
responsive.desktop: Full table with checkboxes. Applied filters show as chips under the toolbar. Preview panel on the right.

states.name: Default
states.what: A row goes to the record page. The icon at the end of a row opens the edit panel instead.

states.name: Edit panel
states.what: Edit in a right panel so the list stays in view. Open full page is the way out when the edit turns out bigger than expected.

states.name: New record modal
states.what: New record is a short modal. It has text fields, so on a phone it takes the whole screen. Only confirmations become bottom sheets.

states.name: Filters panel
states.what: Filters sit in a right panel. The apply button shows the result count. On a phone it takes the whole screen.

templates.interaction: Three ways into one record. Click a row for the full page, click the end icon for a quick edit in a side panel, or use New record for a modal. Pick by size of the task: a few fields is a modal, an edit that needs the list for context is a panel, anything long or linkable is a page.
templates.density_note: Standard by default. A power-user version of this list can switch to Dense.

mobbin_references.title: Calendly contacts
mobbin_references.note: Search, saved view chips, a columns menu, a filter popover, items per page.

responsive.tablet: Three cards per row. Applied filters show as chips above the grid. Filter opens a right drawer.
responsive.desktop: Filter sidebar on the left with four groups. Four cards per row.

states.name: Default

templates.interaction: Filter opens a right drawer on tablet and a full height sheet on a phone. On desktop the sidebar is open by default and Filter shows or hides it, so there is no drawer.

templates.name: Record detail
templates.purpose: One record in a SaaS product, such as a customer, a job, or a service. It shows status and lets people act.
templates.navigation: Breadcrumb back to the list. Tabs split the record into views. Properties sit in a side panel on desktop and fold into a row elsewhere.

responsive.phone: A back link replaces the breadcrumb. The primary action sits under the title and the rest go in an overflow menu. Tabs scroll sideways. Properties fold into one row.
responsive.tablet: Primary action and overflow in the header. Properties fold above the content. Facts go two across.
responsive.desktop: Three actions in the header. Properties panel on the right at 300px. Facts go three across.

states.name: View
states.what: Read mode. Edit sits in the header. One field is clickable to show inline edit.

states.name: Inline edit
states.what: One field turns into an input with its own Save and cancel. Good for a single low stakes change.

states.name: Edit mode
states.what: Every field becomes an input. Save and Cancel replace Edit in the header, and pin to a bar above the tab bar on a phone.

states.name: Discard confirm
states.what: Cancel with unsaved changes asks first. Keep editing is the safe default and also what the scrim does.

templates.interaction: Two ways to edit. Inline edit changes one field in place, with no mode change. Edit mode flips the whole page to inputs. Pick inline when the change is small and safe. Pick the mode when people edit several fields together and need one Save. Cancel with changes always asks before throwing them away.

responsive.tablet: Heading and form side by side. Name and company fields go two across.

templates.name: Data grid
templates.purpose: A dense, spreadsheet-like table for people who live in it all day. Sorting, column control, and bulk edits matter more than looks.
templates.navigation: Same app shell. View tabs sit above the toolbar. Selecting rows swaps in a bulk action bar. Rows open a detail page, not a panel, because the grid already uses the width.

responsive.phone: The grid keeps every column and scrolls sideways inside its card, with the selection box and name pinned on the left. Never hide columns on a table (PATH-B-NARROW). Filter and Sort stay pinned top right as two buttons. Selecting rows shows a bar above the list with one Actions button.
responsive.tablet: All columns stay and the grid scrolls sideways with the name pinned. Toolbar keeps search on the left with Filter and Sort pinned top right, under one view tab row.
responsive.desktop: All columns, a Columns menu, row height control, export, and a bulk action bar above the header when rows are checked. Scrolls sideways when columns outrun the width, with the name column pinned.

states.name: Default
states.what: Rows are checked, so the bulk bar is showing. A row click goes to the record.

states.name: Filter panel
states.what: Filters open in a right panel so the grid stays visible while people tune them.

states.name: Delete confirm
states.what: A destructive bulk action gets a modal that says how many rows it touches. Never delete on the first click.

templates.interaction: Checking rows swaps in the bulk bar. Delete asks for confirmation in a modal that names the count. Filter opens a side panel and keeps the grid on screen. A row click leaves the grid for the record page.
templates.density_note: The densest template here. Desktop rows use the dense height. On touch widths rows return to regular height.

responsive.phone: Each person is a stacked row: avatar and name as the title, with email, role, and status under it. Tapping the row opens the edit panel. Invite stays at the top.
responsive.tablet: Sub-nav becomes tabs across the top. Role shows as a dropdown in the row. Status stays in the row.

states.name: Remove confirm

templates.name: Report table
templates.purpose: A table that summarizes numbers: a date range, a chart, and rows with a totals line. Mostly read, then exported.
templates.navigation: Reports usually have their own sub-list in the sidebar, like Sales summary, Item sales, and Team sales. Date range and grouping sit on the left in a row above the chart. Filter and Sort are pinned top right of it.

responsive.phone: Controls collapse into a date chip and an Options button. The chart shrinks. The table keeps every column, scrolls sideways inside its card, and pins the first column. The page itself never scrolls sideways.
responsive.tablet: Chart on top, table below. All columns stay and the table scrolls sideways with the first column pinned. Numbers right-aligned so they line up.
responsive.desktop: All columns, a bold totals row at the bottom, and Export in the header.

templates.name: Onboarding steps
templates.purpose: A short, focused setup of 2 to 5 steps with a 1-2-3 stepper, shown before or just after the first visit. One question group per step, then into the product.
templates.navigation: No product navigation. A minimal header with the logo and Save and exit, so people stay in the flow. Back goes one step, Next goes forward, and the last step ends in the product. For SaaS, keep this to what the account needs to work, then drop people on the dashboard with a setup checklist.

responsive.phone: Stepper keeps its three markers but drops the labels and adds one line, Step 2 of 3: Goals. Content is one column. Back and Next sit in a sticky bottom bar with Next filling the width, and Skip is a text link above it.
responsive.tablet: Stepper shows markers with labels. Content is centered in a column capped near 560px. Back sits at the far left of the footer and Skip then Next at the far right.
responsive.desktop: Same as tablet with more air around the column. Choice cards go two across. The footer stays under the content, not pinned to the window.

states.name: Step 1
states.what: Required basics only. No Skip, because the account needs these. Back is hidden on the first step.

states.name: Step 2
states.what: Pick one card. Skip is allowed because the answer only tunes suggestions.

states.name: Step 3
states.what: Invite and connect are both optional. The primary button says Finish, not Next.

states.name: Done
states.what: The stepper shows all three as complete. One primary button goes to the dashboard. This screen is not a fourth step.

templates.interaction: Next validates the step, then moves on. Back keeps what was typed. Skip moves on without saving that step. Finish lands on a short done screen, then the dashboard. Save and exit leaves and lets people resume at the same step. Primary is always the rightmost button, with Skip to its left, and Back sits alone at the far left.
templates.density_note: First-run screens get the loosest spacing: one idea per step, a narrow centered column, big gaps around the stepper.
